messages.subject: random coefficients models
parts:
Hello, 
I am a new INLA user, and I have been exploring how to specify some common multilevel models. 

Using these data https://db.tt/PliyNzecVo I run the following model using lmer:

random intercept (schools), IQ random coefficient by school, SES random coefficient by school.  

library(lme4)
library(INLA)

mlbook_red <- read.table("data/mlbook2_r.dat", header=TRUE)

lout3 <- lmer(langPOST ~ 1 + IQ_verb + ses + (IQ_verb + ses|schoolnr),
                data = mlbook_red, REML = FALSE)

     AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid
 24682.0  24744.3 -12331.0  24662.0     3748

Random effects:
 Groups   Name        Variance  Std.Dev. Corr
 schoolnr (Intercept)  9.444821 3.07324
          IQ_verb           0.263086 0.51292  -0.58
          ses                  0.001772 0.04209  -0.17 -0.71
 Residual                   37.221208 6.10092
Number of obs: 3758, groups:  schoolnr, 211

Fixed effects:
            Estimate Std. Error t value
(Intercept) 41.13221    0.23787  172.92
IQ_verb      2.28822    0.06671   34.30
ses          0.16376    0.01149   14.25

I tried to replicate this model using INLA: 

maxsch <- max(mlbook_red$schoolnr)
mlbook_red$schooliq <- mlbook_red$schoolnr + maxsch
mlbook_red$schoolses <- mlbook_red$schoolnr + max(mlbook_red$schooliq)

formula <- langPOST ~ 1 + IQ_verb + ses +
             f(schoolnr, model = "iid3d", n = 3 * maxsch) +
             f(schooliq, IQ_verb, copy = "schoolnr") +
             f(schoolses, ses, copy = "schoolnr")
out4 <- inla(formula,  family = "gaussian", data = mlbook_red)

out4$summary.fixed[, c(1,2, 3, 5)]
                  mean         sd 0.025quant 0.975quant
(Intercept) 41.1859946 0.23895463 40.7150315 41.6539903
IQ_verb     2.2814430 0.06665462  2.1511814  2.4129113
ses            0.1695141 0.01559949  0.1389249  0.2001783

Fixed effects look right. 

inla.contrib.sd(out4) # this doesn't work because of the correlation terms
Error in if (xx[1] > xx[n]) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In sqrt(x) : NaNs produced
2: In sqrt(x) : NaNs produced
3: In sqrt(x) : NaNs produced
4: In sqrt(x) : NaNs produced
5: In sqrt(x) : NaNs produced

residual <- inla.emarginal(function(x) sqrt(1/x), out4$marginals.hyperpar[[1]])
sd_school <- inla.emarginal(function(x) sqrt(1/x), out4$marginals.hyperpar[[2]])
sd_iq <- inla.emarginal(function(x) sqrt(1/x), out4$marginals.hyperpar[[3]])
sd_ses <- inla.emarginal(function(x) sqrt(1/x), out4$marginals.hyperpar[[4]])
rbind(sd_school, sd_iq, sd_ses, residual)

               [,1]
sd_school 3.0012572
sd_iq     0.4895140
sd_ses    0.1413997
residual  6.0866283

The biggest difference is observed in ses (0.042 in lmer versus 0.14 using INLA). 
The correlations looks weird: 

 out4$summary.hyper[5:7, c(1,2)]
                           mean        sd
Rho1:2 for schoolnr -0.58487314 0.1228105 # this seems consistent
Rho1:3 for schoolnr -0.02188838 0.1122993 # versus -0.17 in lmer
Rho2:3 for schoolnr -0.10993718 0.1181757 # versus -0.71 in lmer

I wonder if my specification using INLA is wrong, or if these differences are due to the default priors being used. 

Any suggestions would be appreciated it. 

Thank you, 
Sebastian

something like this. I guess you want to set some decent priors but I
havn't looked into that [please see https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.4630,
which will soon appear in Stat.Sci as a discussion paper],

Best
H

***************************************************

library(lme4)
library(INLA)

mlbook_red <- read.table("data/mlbook2_r.dat", header=TRUE)

lout3 <- lmer(langPOST ~ 1 + IQ_verb + ses + (IQ_verb + ses|schoolnr),
                data = mlbook_red, REML = FALSE)

mlbook_red$schooliq <- mlbook_red$schoolnr
mlbook_red$schoolses <- mlbook_red$schoolnr

formula <- (langPOST ~ 1 + IQ_verb + ses +
                ## set constr=T to avoid confounding with the fixed
effect, but this it not what
                ## is done in lmer() I think.
                f(schoolnr, model="iid",  constr=F) +  
                f(schooliq, IQ_verb, model="iid",  constr=F) +  
                f(schoolses, ses, model="iid", constr=F))

summary(lout3)

## estimated stdev's based on the mode (the 'mean' does not make sense,
why????)
a = sqrt(1/out4$summary.hyperpar[,"mode"])
names(a) = paste("stdev",  c("noise",  "schoolnr", "IQ", "ses"))
print(a)

out4$summary.fixed

On Fri, 2017-02-24 at 08:20 -0800, Sebastián Daza wrote:
> Thanks for your reply, Havard. 
>
> Yes, you're right, I shouldn't use the mean to estimate the stdev of
> the random effects, the distributions are too skewed!

E log(precision) make sense, not E(precision) as the tail can be
serious.

> I still don't get the correlation between intercepts and slopes, that
> is not being estimated, right?
>

if you want this, you have to use another model than iid+iid for the
two you want together.
